sanskrit: athābravīd dvijaḥ kaś cid arjunasya priyaḥ sakhā eṣyatīha mahābāhur vaśī śaurir udāradhīḥ
english: Then a certain brahmin, a dear friend of Arjuna, spoke: 'The mighty-armed one, the self-controlled Śauri of noble intellect, will come here.'

sanskrit: viditā hi harer yūyam ihāyātāḥ kurūdvahāḥ sadā hi darśanākāṅkṣī śreyo 'nveṣī ca vo hariḥ
english: For Hari knows that you, the foremost of the Kurus, have arrived here. Hari always longs to see you and ever seeks your welfare.

sanskrit: bahuvatsarajīvī ca mārkaṇḍeyo mahātapāḥ svādhyāyatapasā yuktaḥ kṣipraṃ yuṣmān sameṣyati
english: And Mārkaṇḍeya, the great ascetic who has lived for many thousands of years, absorbed in self-study and austerity, will soon come to meet you.

sanskrit: tathaiva tasya bruvataḥ pratyadṛṣyata keśavaḥ sainyasugrīvayuktena rathena rathināṃ varaḥ
english: Even as he spoke those words, Keśava appeared — the best of chariot-warriors — his chariot yoked with Sainya and Sugrīva.

sanskrit: maghavān iva paulomyā sahitaḥ satyabhāmayā upāyād devakīputro didṛkṣuḥ kurusattamān
english: Like Maghavān accompanied by the daughter of Puloman, the son of Devakī arrived with Satyabhāmā, eager to behold the best of the Kurus.

sanskrit: avatīrya rathāt kṛṣṇo dharmarājaṃ yathāvidhi vavande mudito dhīmān bhīmaṃ ca balināṃ varam
english: Descending from the chariot, the wise and joyful Kṛṣṇa greeted Dharmarāja with due ceremony and also Bhīma, the foremost among the strong.

sanskrit: pūjayām āsa dhaumyaṃ ca yamābhyām abhivāditaḥ pariṣvajya guḍākeśaṃ draupadīṃ paryasāntvayat
english: He honored Dhaumya as well; having been greeted by the twins, he embraced Guḍākeśa and then consoled Draupadī.

sanskrit: sa dṛṣṭvā phalgunaṃ vīraṃ cirasya priyam āgatam paryaṣvajata dāśārhaḥ punaḥ punar ariṃdamam
english: Seeing the heroic Phalguna, his dear one who had returned after so long, the Dāśārha embraced the subduer of enemies again and again.

sanskrit: tathaiva satyabhāmāpi draupadīṃ pariṣasvaje pāṇḍavānāṃ priyāṃ bhāryāṃ kṛṣṇasya mahiṣī priyā
english: Likewise Satyabhāmā, the beloved queen of Kṛṣṇa, embraced Draupadī, the beloved wife of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: tatas te pāṇḍavāḥ sarve sabhāryāḥ sapurohitāḥ ānarcuḥ puṇḍarīkākṣaṃ parivavruś ca sarvaśaḥ
english: Then all the Pāṇḍavas, together with their wives and their family priest, honored the lotus-eyed one and surrounded him on all sides.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇas tu pārthena sametya vidvān; dhanaṃjayenāsuratarjanena babhau yathā bhūtapatir mahātmā; sametya sākṣād bhagavān guhena
english: The wise Kṛṣṇa, having united with Pārtha — the terror of demons — shone like the great-souled lord of beings, Bhagavān himself meeting with Guha face to face.

sanskrit: tataḥ samastāni kirīṭamālī; vaneṣu vṛttāni gadāgrajāya uktvā yathāvat punar anvapṛcchat; kathaṃ subhadrā ca tathābhimanyuḥ
english: Then the diadem-wearer, having duly related all that had transpired in the forests to the elder brother of Gada, inquired in return: 'How is Subhadrā, and how is Abhimanyu?'

sanskrit: sa pūjayitvā madhuhā yathāvat; pārthāṃś ca kṛṣṇāṃ ca purohitaṃ ca uvāca rājānam abhipraśaṃsan; yudhiṣṭhiraṃ tatra sahopaviśya
english: Then the slayer of Madhu, having duly honored the Pārthas, Kṛṣṇā, and the family priest, sat down beside King Yudhiṣṭhira and addressed him with words of praise.

sanskrit: dharmaḥ paraḥ pāṇḍava rājyalābhāt; tasyārtham āhus tapa eva rājan satyārjavābhyāṃ caratā svadharmaṃ; jitas tavāyaṃ ca paraś ca lokaḥ
english: 'Dharma is higher than the gaining of a kingdom, O Pāṇḍava; for its sake they speak of austerity alone, O king. Practicing your own dharma with truth and straightforwardness, you have conquered both this world and the next.'

sanskrit: adhītam agre caratā vratāni; samyag dhanurvedam avāpya kṛtsnam kṣātreṇa dharmeṇa vasūni labdhvā; sarve hy avāptāḥ kratavaḥ purāṇāḥ
english: 'In the beginning you studied while observing vows; having fully mastered the science of archery and acquired wealth through kṣatriya dharma — all the ancient sacrifices have indeed been accomplished by you.'

sanskrit: na grāmyadharmeṣu ratis tavāsti; kāmān na kiṃ cit kuruṣe narendra na cārthalobhāt prajahāsi dharmaṃ; tasmāt svabhāvād asi dharmarājaḥ
english: 'You have no delight in the vulgar duties, O lord of men; you pursue no desires whatsoever, nor do you abandon dharma out of greed for wealth — therefore by your very nature you are Dharmarāja.'

sanskrit: dānaṃ ca satyaṃ ca tapaś ca rājañ; śraddhā ca śāntiś ca dhṛtiḥ kṣamā ca avāpya rāṣṭrāṇi vasūni bhogān; eṣā parā pārtha sadā ratis te
english: 'Charity, truth, austerity, O king — faith, peace, fortitude, and forbearance — having acquired kingdoms, wealth, and pleasures, these are ever your supreme delight, O Pārtha.'

sanskrit: yadā janaughaḥ kurujāṅgalānāṃ; kṛṣṇāṃ sabhāyām avaśām apaśyat apetadharmavyavahāravṛttaṃ; saheta tat pāṇḍava kas tvad anyaḥ
english: 'When the multitude of the Kurujāṅgalas witnessed Kṛṣṇā helpless in the assembly hall — conduct wholly devoid of the practice of dharma — who other than you, O Pāṇḍava, could have endured that?'

sanskrit: asaṃśayaṃ sarvasamṛddhakāmaḥ; kṣipraṃ prajāḥ pālayitāsi samyak ime vayaṃ nigrahaṇe kurūṇāṃ; yadi pratijñā bhavataḥ samāptā
english: 'Without doubt, with all desires fulfilled, you will soon rightfully protect your subjects. We are here for the subjugation of the Kurus — if your vow is completed.'

sanskrit: dhaumyaṃ ca kṛṣṇāṃ ca yudhiṣṭhiraṃ ca; yamau ca bhīmaṃ ca daśārhasiṃhaḥ uvāca diṣṭyā bhavatāṃ śivena; prāptaḥ kirīṭī muditaḥ kṛtāstraḥ
english: The lion of the Dāśārhas addressed Dhaumya, Kṛṣṇā, Yudhiṣṭhira, the twins, and Bhīma: 'By fortune, the diadem-wearer has arrived to your auspicious company — joyful and his weapons mastered.'

sanskrit: provāca kṛṣṇām api yājñasenīṃ; daśārhabhartā sahitaḥ suhṛdbhiḥ kṛṣṇe dhanurvedaratipradhānāḥ; satyavratās te śiśavaḥ suśīlāḥ sadbhiḥ sadaivācaritaṃ samādhiṃ; caranti putrās tava yājñaseni
english: The lord of the Dāśārhas also spoke to Kṛṣṇā Yājñasenī, surrounded by his friends: 'O Kṛṣṇe, your sons — devoted chiefly to the science of archery, steadfast in their vows, of good character — ever practice the concentration always cultivated by the virtuous, O Yājñasenī.'

sanskrit: rājyena rāṣṭraiś ca nimantryamāṇāḥ; pitrā ca kṛṣṇe tava sodaraiś ca na yajñasenasya na mātulānāṃ; gṛheṣu bālā ratim āpnuvanti
english: 'Though invited with kingdoms and realms by their father and by your brothers, O Kṛṣṇe, your sons do not find delight dwelling in the houses of Yajñasena or of their maternal uncles.'

sanskrit: ānartam evābhimukhāḥ śivena; gatvā dhanurvedaratipradhānāḥ tavātmajā vṛṣṇipuraṃ praviśya; na daivatebhyaḥ spṛhayanti kṛṣṇe
english: 'With auspicious intent they face Ānarta; your sons, devoted chiefly to the science of archery, having gone and entered the city of the Vṛṣṇis, do not envy even the gods, O Kṛṣṇe.'

sanskrit: yathā tvam evārhasi teṣu vṛttiṃ; prayoktum āryā ca yathaiva kuntī teṣv apramādena sadā karoti; tathā ca bhūyaś ca tathā subhadrā
english: 'Just as you yourself are worthy of rendering your conduct toward them, and just as the noble Kuntī always tends to them with care — so too does Subhadrā, and even more so.'

sanskrit: yathāniruddhasya yathābhimanyor; yathā sunīthasya yathaiva bhānoḥ tathā vinetā ca gatiś ca kṛṣṇe; tavātmajānām api raukmiṇeyaḥ
english: 'As he is to Aniruddha, as he is to Abhimanyu, as he is to Sunītha, and as he is to Bhānu — so too is the son of Rukmiṇī the guide and protector of your sons, O Kṛṣṇe.'

sanskrit: gadāsicarmagrahaṇeṣu śūrān; astreṣu śikṣāsu rathāśvayāne samyag vinetā vinayaty atandrīs; tāṃś cābhimanyuḥ satataṃ kumāraḥ
english: 'He tirelessly and properly trains those heroes in the wielding of maces, swords, and shields, in missile-lore and instruction, and in chariot and horse-riding; and the young Abhimanyu trains them constantly as well.'

sanskrit: sa cāpi samyak praṇidhāya śikṣām; astrāṇi caiṣāṃ guruvat pradāya tavātmajānāṃ ca tathābhimanyoḥ; parākramais tuṣyati raukmiṇeyaḥ
english: 'And he too, having properly imparted the training and the weapons to your sons like a teacher, rejoices in the feats of valor of both your sons and Abhimanyu — so says the son of Rukmiṇī.'

sanskrit: yadā vihāraṃ prasamīkṣamāṇāḥ; prayānti putrās tava yājñaseni ekaikam eṣām anuyānti tatra; rathāś ca yānāni ca dantinaś ca
english: 'Whenever your sons set out for recreation, O Yājñasenī, chariots, vehicles, and elephants follow behind each and every one of them.'

sanskrit: athābravīd dharmarājaṃ tu kṛṣṇo; daśārhayodhāḥ kukurāndhakāś ca ete nideśaṃ tava pālayanti; tiṣṭhanti yatrecchasi tatra rājan
english: Then Kṛṣṇa spoke to Dharmarāja: 'The warriors of the Dāśārhas, the Kukuras and the Andhakas — these all observe your command; they stand wherever you wish them to stand, O king.'

sanskrit: āvartatāṃ kārmukavegavātā; halāyudhapragrahaṇā madhūnām senā tavārtheṣu narendra yattā; sasādipattyaśvarathā sanāgā
english: 'Let the army of the Madhus be set in motion — swept by the wind of bowstring-speed, guided by the grasp of the Ploughshare-wielder — ready for your purposes, O lord of men, with cavalry, infantry, horses, chariots, and elephants.'

sanskrit: prasthāpyatāṃ pāṇḍava dhārtarāṣṭraḥ; suyodhanaḥ pāpakṛtāṃ variṣṭhaḥ sa sānubandhaḥ sasuhṛdgaṇaś ca; saubhasya saubhādhipateś ca mārgam
english: 'Let the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra be sent forth, O Pāṇḍava — Suyodhana, foremost among evildoers — along with his relatives and his multitude of allies, along the path of Saubha and the lord of Saubha.'

sanskrit: kāmaṃ tathā tiṣṭha narendra tasmin; yathā kṛtas te samayaḥ sabhāyām dāśārhayodhais tu sasādiyodhaṃ; pratīkṣatāṃ nāgapuraṃ bhavantam
english: 'Stay there as long as you wish, O lord of men, according to the agreement you made in the assembly; but let Nāgapura await you with the Dāśārha warriors and their cavalry-fighters.'

sanskrit: vyapetamanyur vyapanītapāpmā; vihṛtya yatrecchasi tatra kāmam tataḥ samṛddhaṃ prathamaṃ viśokaḥ; prapatsyase nāgapuraṃ sarāṣṭram
english: 'With your anger gone and your sin removed, roam wherever you desire at will; thereafter, free from sorrow and in fullness, you shall first attain Nāgapura together with its realm.'

sanskrit: tatas tad ājñāya mataṃ mahātmā; yathāvad uktaṃ puruṣottamena praśasya viprekṣya ca dharmarājaḥ; kṛtāñjaliḥ keśavam ity uvāca
english: Then the great-souled Dharmarāja, having understood and duly considered the opinion expressed by the best of men, praised it and with hands folded in reverence spoke to Keśava thus:

sanskrit: asaṃśayaṃ keśava pāṇḍavānāṃ; bhavān gatis tvaccharaṇā hi pārthāḥ kālodaye tac ca tataś ca bhūyaḥ; kartā bhavān karma na saṃśayo 'sti
english: 'Without doubt, O Keśava, you are the refuge of the Pāṇḍavas; the Pārthas seek shelter in you. When the time arrives, you will accomplish that and more — of this there is no doubt.'

sanskrit: yathāpratijñaṃ vihṛtaś ca kālaḥ; sarvāḥ samā dvādaśa nirjaneṣu ajñātacaryāṃ vidhivat samāpya; bhavadgatāḥ keśava pāṇḍaveyāḥ
english: 'The time has been spent as pledged; all twelve years in the wilderness have been passed, and after duly completing the year of incognito life, the sons of Pāṇḍu will come to you, O Keśava.'

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tathā vadati vārṣṇeye dharmarāje ca bhārata atha paścāt tapovṛddho bahuvarṣasahasradhṛk pratyadṛṣyata dharmātmā mārkaṇḍeyo mahātapāḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: While the Vṛṣṇi lord and Dharmarāja were thus speaking, O Bhārata, thereafter appeared the righteous-souled Mārkaṇḍeya of great austerity — grown aged by austerity, the bearer of thousands upon thousands of years.

sanskrit: tam āgatam ṛṣiṃ vṛddhaṃ bahuvarṣasahasriṇam ānarcur brāhmaṇāḥ sarve kṛṣṇaś ca saha pāṇḍavaiḥ
english: All the brahmins honored that arriving sage, aged with thousands upon thousands of years, and so did Kṛṣṇa together with the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: tam arcitaṃ suviṣvastam āsīnam ṛṣisattamam brāhmaṇānāṃ matenāha pāṇḍavānāṃ ca keśavaḥ
english: When that best of sages had been honored and sat at ease, Keśava spoke — in accord with the minds of the brahmins and the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: śuśrūṣavaḥ pāṇḍavās te brāhmaṇāś ca samāgatāḥ draupadī satyabhāmā ca tathāhaṃ paramaṃ vacaḥ
english: 'These Pāṇḍavas are eager to hear, and the brahmins have assembled; Draupadī, Satyabhāmā, and I likewise — all desire your supreme words.'

sanskrit: purāvṛttāḥ kathāḥ puṇyāḥ sadācārāḥ sanātanāḥ rājñāṃ strīṇām ṛṣīṇāṃ ca mārkaṇḍeya vicakṣva naḥ
english: 'Holy tales of ancient times, the eternal customs of right conduct of kings, women, and sages — O Mārkaṇḍeya, declare these to us.'

sanskrit: teṣu tatropaviṣṭeṣu devarṣir api nāradaḥ ājagāma viśuddhātmā pāṇḍavān avalokakaḥ
english: While they were seated there, the divine seer Nārada too arrived — of pure soul — to behold the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: tam apy atha mahātmānaṃ sarve tu puruṣarṣabhāḥ pādyārghyābhyāṃ yathānyāyam upatasthur manīṣiṇam
english: All those bulls among men then duly attended that great-souled and wise one as well, with water for the feet and the guest-offering, according to proper rite.

sanskrit: nāradas tv atha devarṣir jñātvā tāṃs tu kṛtakṣaṇān mārkaṇḍeyasya vadatas tāṃ kathām anvamodata
english: Then the divine seer Nārada, perceiving that they were in an appropriate moment, approved of the discourse that Mārkaṇḍeya was about to deliver.

sanskrit: uvāca cainaṃ kālajñaḥ smayann iva sa nāradaḥ brahmarṣe kathyatāṃ yat te pāṇḍaveṣu vivakṣitam
english: And that Nārada, knower of the right time, spoke to him with something like a smile: 'O brahmin-seer, let what you desire to say to the Pāṇḍavas be told.'

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ pratyuvāca mārkaṇḍeyo mahātapāḥ kṣaṇaṃ kurudhvaṃ vipulam ākhyātavyaṃ bhaviṣyati
english: Thus addressed, Mārkaṇḍeya of great austerity replied: 'Allow an ample moment — much will need to be narrated.'

sanskrit: evam uktāḥ kṣaṇaṃ cakruḥ pāṇḍavāḥ saha tair dvijaiḥ madhyaṃdine yathādityaṃ prekṣantas taṃ mahāmunim
english: Thus addressed, the Pāṇḍavas together with those brahmins fell silent for a moment, gazing upon that great sage as one gazes at the midday sun.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca taṃ vivakṣantam ālakṣya kururājo mahāmunim kathāsaṃjananārthāya codayām āsa pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Perceiving that great sage ready to speak, the Kuru king, the son of Pāṇḍu, urged him on in order to give rise to the discourse.

sanskrit: bhavān daivatadaityānām ṛṣīṇāṃ ca mahātmanām rājarṣīṇāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ caritajñaḥ sanātanaḥ
english: 'You are the eternal knower of the deeds of gods and demons, of great-souled seers, and of all royal sages.'

sanskrit: sevyaś copāsitavyaś ca mato naḥ kāṅkṣitaś ciram ayaṃ ca devakīputraḥ prāpto 'smān avalokakaḥ
english: 'You are worthy of service and veneration in our eyes, long desired by us. And this son of Devakī has arrived to behold us.'

sanskrit: bhavaty eva hi me buddhir dṛṣṭvātmānaṃ sukhāc cyutam dhārtarāṣṭrāṃś ca durvṛttān ṛdhyataḥ prekṣya sarvaśaḥ
english: 'Indeed my mind becomes troubled when I see myself fallen from happiness and behold the ill-behaved sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra prospering in every way.'

sanskrit: karmaṇaḥ puruṣaḥ kartā śubhasyāpy aśubhasya ca svaphalaṃ tad upāśnāti kathaṃ kartā svid īśvaraḥ
english: 'A person is the doer of his action, whether auspicious or inauspicious, and he reaps the fruit thereof — how then is the agent himself an independent lord?'

sanskrit: atha vā sukhaduḥkheṣu nṛṇāṃ brahmavidāṃ vara iha vā kṛtam anveti paradehe 'tha vā punaḥ
english: 'Or, O best among knowers of Brahman, does what is done here follow men in their pleasure and pain into another body, or yet again in this very life?'

sanskrit: dehī ca dehaṃ saṃtyajya mṛgyamāṇaḥ śubhāśubhaiḥ kathaṃ saṃyujyate pretya iha vā dvijasattama
english: 'And when the embodied soul abandons the body — pursued by auspicious and inauspicious deeds — how does it become united with them after death, or in this very life, O best of twice-born?'

sanskrit: aihalaukikam evaitad utāho pāralaukikam kva ca karmāṇi tiṣṭhanti jantoḥ pretasya bhārgava
english: 'Is this pertaining only to this world or also to the next? And where do the deeds of a creature abide after it has died, O descendant of Bhṛgu?'

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca tvadyukto 'yam anupraśno yathāvad vadatāṃ vara viditaṃ veditavyaṃ te sthityartham anupṛcchasi
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: 'This supplementary inquiry befits you, O best among speakers. What needs to be known is already known to you; you ask in order to understand the principle rightly.'

sanskrit: atra te vartayiṣyāmi tad ihaikamanāḥ śṛṇu yathehāmutra ca naraḥ sukhaduḥkham upāśnute
english: 'On this I will instruct you — listen here with one-pointed mind — how a person experiences pleasure and pain both in this world and in the next.'

sanskrit: nirmalāni śarīrāṇi viśuddhāni śarīriṇām sasarja dharmatantrāṇi pūrvotpannaḥ prajāpatiḥ
english: 'Prajāpati, born before all others, fashioned the bodies of embodied beings as pure and spotless, bound by the web of dharma.'

sanskrit: amoghabalasaṃkalpāḥ suvratāḥ satyavādinaḥ brahmabhūtā narāḥ puṇyāḥ purāṇāḥ kurunandana
english: 'Those ancient, holy men had infallible strength and purpose, were of excellent vows, spoke truth, had become one with Brahman — O joy of the Kurus.'

sanskrit: sarve devaiḥ samāyānti svacchandena nabhastalam tataś ca punar āyānti sarve svacchandacāriṇaḥ
english: 'All of them would rise with the gods of their own free will into the sky, and they would all come back again, moving freely at will.'

sanskrit: svacchandamaraṇāś cāsan narāḥ svacchandajīvinaḥ alpabādhā nirātaṅkā siddhārthā nirupadravāḥ
english: 'Men died at will and lived at will; they had little affliction, were free from distress, their purposes accomplished, undisturbed by calamities.'

sanskrit: draṣṭāro devasaṃghānām ṛṣīṇāṃ ca mahātmanām pratyakṣāḥ sarvadharmāṇāṃ dāntā vigatamatsarāḥ
english: 'They were seers of assemblies of gods and of great-souled sages; all dharmas were direct and manifest to them; they were self-restrained and free from envy.'

sanskrit: āsan varṣasahasrāṇi tathā putrasahasriṇaḥ tataḥ kālāntare 'nyasmin pṛthivītalacāriṇaḥ
english: 'They lived for thousands of years, and likewise had thousands of sons. Then, in another age, they became wanderers on the surface of the earth.'

sanskrit: kāmakrodhābhibhūtās te māyāvyājopajīvinaḥ lobhamohābhibhūtāś ca tyaktā devais tato narāḥ
english: 'Overcome by desire and wrath, living by deceit and fraud, overwhelmed by greed and delusion — those men were then abandoned by the gods.'

sanskrit: aśubhaiḥ karmabhiḥ pāpās tiryaṅ narakagāminaḥ saṃsāreṣu vicitreṣu pacyamānāḥ punaḥ punaḥ
english: 'Sinful through inauspicious deeds, destined for animal births and hell, they were cooked again and again in the varied rounds of transmigration.'

sanskrit: mogheṣṭā moghasaṃkalpā moghajñānā vicetasaḥ sarvātiśaṅkinaś caiva saṃvṛttāḥ kleśabhāginaḥ aśubhaiḥ karmabhiś cāpi prāyaśaḥ paricihnitāḥ
english: 'Their desires were vain, their purposes vain, their knowledge vain; they were witless, filled with excessive suspicion, burdened with affliction, and mostly marked by inauspicious deeds.'

sanskrit: dauṣkulyā vyādhibahulā durātmāno 'pratāpinaḥ bhavanty alpāyuṣaḥ pāpā raudrakarmaphalodayāḥ nāthantaḥ sarvakāmānāṃ nāstikā bhinnasetavaḥ
english: 'Of base lineage, afflicted by many diseases, evil-souled, causing no remorse to others, they become short-lived sinners bearing the fruit of terrible deeds — seekers of all desires, unbelievers, breakers of sacred bonds.'

sanskrit: jantoḥ pretasya kaunteya gatiḥ svair iha karmabhiḥ prājñasya hīnabuddheś ca karmakośaḥ kva tiṣṭhati
english: 'The course of a creature after death is determined by its own deeds here, O son of Kuntī — but where does the storehouse of karma abide, for the wise man and for the man of poor understanding alike?'

sanskrit: kvasthas tat samupāśnāti sukṛtaṃ yadi vetarat iti te darśanaṃ yac ca tatrāpy anunayaṃ śṛṇu
english: 'And dwelling where does it experience the merit or the demerit? This is your question — and hear now on that point also the elucidation.'

sanskrit: ayam ādiśarīreṇa devasṛṣṭena mānavaḥ śubhānām aśubhānāṃ ca kurute saṃcayaṃ mahat
english: 'This human being, with the primal body created by the gods, accumulates a great store of both auspicious and inauspicious deeds.'

sanskrit: āyuṣo 'nte prahāyedaṃ kṣīṇaprāyaṃ kalevaram saṃbhavaty eva yugapad yonau nāsty antarābhavaḥ
english: 'At the end of life, abandoning this nearly exhausted body, it comes into being simultaneously in the womb — there is no intermediate existence.'

sanskrit: tatrāsya svakṛtaṃ karma chāyevānugataṃ sadā phalaty atha sukhārho vā duḥkhārho vāpi jāyate
english: 'There its self-wrought karma, ever following it like a shadow, bears fruit; and so it is born worthy of happiness or worthy of suffering.'

sanskrit: kṛtāntavidhisaṃyuktaḥ sa jantur lakṣaṇaiḥ śubhaiḥ aśubhair vā nirādāno lakṣyate jñānadṛṣṭibhiḥ
english: 'That creature, conjoined with the ordinance of Fate, is perceived — endowed with auspicious or inauspicious marks, without disguise — by those possessed of the eye of knowledge.'

sanskrit: eṣā tāvad abuddhīnāṃ gatir uktā yudhiṣṭhira ataḥ paraṃ jñānavatāṃ nibodha gatim uttamām
english: 'This then is the course stated for the unintelligent, O Yudhiṣṭhira. Beyond this, understand now the supreme course of those endowed with knowledge.'

sanskrit: manuṣyās taptatapasaḥ sarvāgamaparāyaṇāḥ sthiravratāḥ satyaparā guruśuśrūṣaṇe ratāḥ
english: 'Men who have practiced austerities, devoted to all the sacred scriptures, firm in their vows, intent on truth, delighting in service to the teacher —'

sanskrit: suśīlāḥ śuklajātīyāḥ kṣāntā dāntāḥ sutejasaḥ śubhayonyantaragatāḥ prāyaśaḥ śubhalakṣaṇāḥ
english: '— of good character, of a pure caste, patient, self-controlled, of excellent splendor, who have passed through a succession of auspicious wombs — mostly bear auspicious marks.'

sanskrit: jitendriyatvād vaśinaḥ śuklatvān mandarogiṇaḥ alpabādhaparitrāsād bhavanti nirupadravāḥ
english: 'Through mastery of the senses they are self-controlled; through their purity they suffer little illness; through having little affliction and fear they are free from calamities.'

sanskrit: cyavantaṃ jāyamānaṃ ca garbhasthaṃ caiva sarvaśaḥ svam ātmānaṃ paraṃ caiva budhyante jñānacakṣuṣaḥ karmabhūmim imāṃ prāpya punar yānti surālayam
english: 'With the eye of knowledge they perceive in every way their own self and the supreme self — departing, being born, and even while in the womb; and having reached this field of action, they return again to the abode of the gods.'

sanskrit: kiṃ cid daivād dhaṭhāt kiṃ cit kiṃ cid eva svakarmabhiḥ prāpnuvanti narā rājan mā te 'stv anyā vicāraṇā
english: 'Men attain things partly through fate, partly through perseverance, and partly through their own deeds, O king — let there be no other consideration in your mind.'

sanskrit: imām atropamāṃ cāpi nibodha vadatāṃ vara manuṣyaloke yac chreyaḥ paraṃ manye yudhiṣṭhira
english: 'And understand also this simile regarding this — O best among speakers — what I consider the supreme good in the world of men, O Yudhiṣṭhira.'
